morphology.capsule: Mucoid polysaccharide (alginate) capsule in some strains, especially cystic fibrosis isolates
morphology.motility: Motile via a single polar flagellum

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, water, and other moist environments
habitat.hostAssociation: Opportunistic pathogen in immunocompromised, burn, and cystic fibrosis patients
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Ubiquitous in moist environments — sinks, hospital equipment, humidifiers

culture.media: MacConkey agar (non-lactose fermenter), routine nutrient agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe; notably grows at 42°C, which helps distinguish it from other Pseudomonas species
culture.colonyMorphology: Flat, spreading colonies with a characteristic grape-like or corn-tortilla odor
culture.pigmentation: Blue-green pigment (pyocyanin) and yellow-green fluorescent pigment (pyoverdine)

identificationClues: Oxidase positive — distinguishes it from most Enterobacteriaceae

diseases: Chronic lung infections in cystic fibrosis
Malignant otitis externa in diabetic patients
virulenceFactors: Pyocyanin — pigment that generates reactive oxygen species
Exotoxin A — inhibits protein synthesis, mechanism similar to diphtheria toxin
Alginate biofilm — drives chronic cystic fibrosis lung infections
clinicalImportance.transmission: Opportunistic — spreads from environmental or hospital reservoirs to susceptible hosts with breaks in skin, immunosuppression, or mechanical ventilation
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Leading cause of hospital-acquired infections in burn units and ICUs; major driver of morbidity and mortality in cystic fibrosis
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Oxidase positivity and pigment production are the key rapid identifiers at the bench

examFacts.importantDisease: Hospital-acquired pneumonia; chronic CF lung infections; burn wound infections
examFacts.importantTest: Oxidase test; blue-green pigment on culture
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Blue-green pyocyanin pigment with a grape-like odor and oxidase positivity
